s.n: Comedy club masala fries with mint yoghurt
s.note: Kumail's stand-up nights at the comedy club
s.how: Heat the oven to 220C. Cut 1kg potatoes into thin chips, soak 20 minutes, drain and dry well. Toss with 3 tbsp oil and roast 35 minutes on lined trays, turning once, until crisp. Toss hot with 2 tsp chaat masala, half a tsp chilli powder, salt and the juice of half a lime. Scatter with chopped coriander and finely diced red onion. Blend 200g Greek yoghurt with a handful of mint and a pinch of salt for dipping.

Boil and crush 600g potatoes with 150g peas, fried onion and a spoon of garam masala. Cut spring roll pastry into strips, fill and fold into triangles. Fry at 180C until crisp. Blitz mint and coriander with a little water, lemon and salt for chutney.

m.note: the family dinners Kumail's mum keeps setting up
m.how: Marinate 1kg chicken thighs in yoghurt and garam masala for 2 hours. Fry 2 sliced onions until crisp. Par-cook 400g basmati for 5 minutes. Layer chicken, rice and onions in a pot, drizzle with saffron soaked in warm milk, seal and bake at 170C for 45 minutes.

w.how: Simmer 100g basmati rice in 1.5L milk over low heat, stirring often, for 45 minutes until thick and creamy. Stir in 100g sugar and a pinch of ground cardamom. Serve warm or chilled with chopped pistachios scattered on top.

d.how: Bring 500ml water to the boil with sliced ginger, a few crushed cardamom pods and a cinnamon stick. Add 4 black tea bags and simmer 2 minutes. Pour in 500ml milk and raw sugar to taste, simmer 5 minutes more and strain into cups.
